question: With the same agent, model and tasks, what changes between OpenCU and iFurySt/open-computer-use 1.1.2 (npm, default settings)?

compared.open-computer-use: 1.1.2 from npm, default settings (no global pointer fallbacks, no Locked Use)

OpenCU.windows: 0.5.0 (the Windows package attached to the v0.6.0 release)
OpenCU.macos: 0.2.0 fix build b975d29, already installed in the benchmark VM; not the current release

linux.desktop: Debian 12 XFCE container, Firefox ESR, Mousepad; fresh container per trial; both arms ran in parallel on the same host
linux.agent: dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 headless, gemini-3.8-flash-high; each arm = shell, files, screenshots plus one engine over stdio MCP
linux.metrics: median per task; inputTokens summed over model steps

tasks.t1-crm: register three customers through a two-step browser wizard
tasks.t2-unsaved: fix a date in an unsaved Mousepad note and save it
tasks.t4-research: look up a year in Firefox and write it to a file
tasks.t5-chart: find the top month of a canvas chart and save it through Mousepad

observed: open-computer-use did not list Firefox until the agent enabled the AT-SPI bus itself (org.a11y.Status) or restarted Firefox with GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY=1; OpenCU enables the bus.

In t1 trial 1, open-computer-use set_value and type_text on the Firefox name and phone entries returned without an error and the entries stayed empty; the agent pasted through the clipboard instead. That trial hit the 900-second limit.
open-computer-use exits without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; the container wrapper supplied one for it.

windows.machine: Windows 11 VM, controller reaches it over wanctl
windows.agent: pi with deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017; each arm = shell and screenshots plus one engine

tasks.t05: enter 10 records in a WinForms form
tasks.t06: go through an NSIS installer wizard
tasks.t07: save a Notepad file as ANSI through Save As
tasks.t08: enter records while a popup interrupts

observed: In all 8 open-computer-use trials the agent also wrote its own Win32 input code (WM_SETTEXT, BM_CLICK, SendInput or SendKeys); the 4 passes completed input that way. In the 8 OpenCU trials it wrote none.

open-computer-use exposes MCP element indices per process, so the bench kept one open-computer-use.exe mcp process on the VM behind a bridge (about 1.5 to 7 s per call); this slows its timings, not its pass count.
Five other trials were discarded and rerun for both arms: a gateway connection reset, Defender quarantining the test installer, and Defender removing wanctl.exe on the VM.

macos.benchmark: MacArena (MacPaw) local subset at upstream dcdc7d36, the 10 tasks that produced grades in earlier runs; original setup commands and graders
macos.machine: macOS 15.6.1 VM, fresh clone per trial, 2 CPU / 6 GiB
macos.agent: OMP 18.8.7 with deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017; 60 requests and 900 s per task; the agent only had the engine

limits: Two trials per cell on Linux and Windows, one on macOS; one model per platform; the macOS OpenCU arm is an older build. Not tested: open-computer-use Locked Use, its SkyLight background input on occluded Chrome windows, and its global pointer fallback setting.
